sheet-3-1.description: Sheet 3, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the northern edge of Vineland just above the borough limits on Cambridge Avenue, between Park Drive on the left and the Central Railroad of New Jersey (Southern Division) on the right. The upper left is a residential district of blocks 85 and 86 cut diagonally by Division Avenue, Fowler Avenue and Crystal Avenue, with frame dwellings, auto houses, a poultry house and lots numbered 2501 to 2538 along Fowler Avenue. The rest of the sheet is filled by the works of the Kimble Glass Co in block 84, between Crystal Avenue and the railroad sidings: the machine shop and machine building, the graduating, packing and lamp rooms, two glass factories with lehrs and furnaces, a batch room, laboratory, carpenter shop, engine room, a 75,000 gallon water tank, a producer house, the long tube machine building and several large warehouses, with a note on watchmen, lighting, power, heat and the private water supply from an artesian well. Railroad sidings run through the works from the main line, which crosses the lower right corner beside a storage yard for old iron, rubber and junk. Along Park Drive and Crystal Avenue in the lower left are rows of dwellings in block 1A. New Street crosses at the upper right, where heavy lines mark the edge of sheet 2. A small boxed inset at the top, with its own north arrow, shows another piece of block 84 (part 2, not placed).
notes: Division Avenue is today Division Street; Cambridge Avenue is Cambridge Street.
The junction of Cambridge Avenue and Harvard Street was hand-picked; north of Cambridge Avenue Harvard is not drawn.
map, 50 ft: Kimble Glass Co between Crystal Av and the Central RR of NJ; Division Av, Fowler Av, Park Drive, Cambridge Av, New; small boxed inset at top (block 84) with its own north arrow.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: boxed inset at the top: piece of block 84 with storage building No 34, own north arrow (no street junction; needs carried points from sheet-3-1 or sheet-2 if the piece can be identified).

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows the north edge of Vineland's centre at 50 ft to an inch, from Park Avenue at the top, where a Boro Limits line follows the street, to Plum at the foot, and from North 4th Street at the left to North West Boulevard and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad at the right, with North East Boulevard just beyond the railroad. Three rows of blocks lie between Park, Peach, Pear and Plum. The upper block is mostly frame dwellings with outbuildings and open lots, the Vineland Pure Milk Co with its milk depot, wagon shed and cement-floored plant at the north end, and Beltch & Barkin, clothing manufacturers, on the west side. The middle row has a large warehouse and repair shop group belonging to Bartholomew & Co, electro plating, a machine shop and an auto repair garage, and dwellings along North West Boulevard. The Central Railroad of New Jersey (New Jersey South Division) runs along the line of Pear Street and crosses the boulevard, and a branch curves in from the right to a siding serving the Lampert Bros pure food products, warehouse and canning plant on the lower block, which also holds a plumbing supplies and glass novelties building, a pipe shed, a printer and a private hay barn. Water pipes of 4 to 10 inches are marked in the streets, with fire hydrants and a fire alarm box. The compass and the Vineland oval stamp fill the right margin, and blocks on the left and right edges belong to neighbouring sheets.
notes: Park Av is today West Park Avenue west of North West Boulevard and East Park Avenue east of it.
The railroad drawn along Pear Street and across North West Boulevard is the Central Railroad of New Jersey, New Jersey South Division; Pear Street junctions were not used for control.
Park Avenue is 100 ft wide on this sheet and the Boro Limits line runs down its centre.
map, 50 ft: Park Av (borough limits line) to Plum, N 4th St to N W Boulevard; CRR of NJ tracks in Pear St (Pear left out).

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the blocks between North East Boulevard at the left edge and North 6th Street, from Park Avenue at the top to Plum at the foot, at 50 ft to an inch. A broad fan of Central Railroad of New Jersey tracks (New Jersey South Division) enters at the lower left and sweeps diagonally to the upper right, cutting across Peach and Pear and dividing the sheet into an industrial centre and residential corners. West of the tracks stand the New Jersey Gas Co works with its retort house, engine room and two iron gas tanks, and next to it the Doerr Glass Co plant, not in operation, with vacuum buildings, lamp room and an office. Ponds Coal & Wood Yard, the Texaco Oil Co and the H. S. Fox Lumber Yard with lumber sheds and a box shook factory occupy the block along the boulevard, with sidings branching from the main line. Between the tracks and North 6th Street are the passenger station and the Central Ice & Cold Storage Co. In the top right, past a foundry and machine shop (not in operation), stand the Blaisdell Machine Works Inc, a grain elevator and grain warehouse beside the tracks, and the Sayford Paper Specialty Co and a garage. The lower blocks hold dwellings, auto repair, a milk house and a playground. Water pipes, hydrants and a fire alarm box are marked, and the compass rose stands near the centre of the top margin.
notes: Park Av is today East Park Avenue; the junction with North East Boulevard lies at or past the left edge.
The railroad crossing Peach and Pear is the Central Railroad of New Jersey, New Jersey South Division; the rail crossings carry less weight than street junctions.
Park Avenue is drawn 100 ft wide here.
map, 50 ft: Park to Plum, N E Boulevard to N 6th St; CRR of NJ diagonal and passenger station.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 lies east of sheet 5 at 50 ft to an inch, between North 7th Street, near the left-centre, and North 8th Street at the right edge, from Park Avenue at the top to Plum at the foot, with the strip between the railroad and North 7th Street to the left. The upper left is crossed by the tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey (Southern Division), which fan out beside the C.R.R. of N.J. Freight Station, a long building angled along the tracks, and the sheet's compass stands in the blank ground beside it. Close to the tracks are the New Bethel A.M.E. Church and dwellings in the block west of North 7th Street. East of North 7th Street the northern block holds a flour and feed warehouse, two warehouses and storage buildings for fruit baskets, auto repair shops, a welding shop and many dwellings and sheds, with a few vacant lots. Between Peach and Pear stand mainly dwellings, the Seventh Day Adventist Church and a vending shop. West of North 7th Street lower blocks hold dwellings and the 1st Church of Christ Scientist, and the south-east block has the Vineland Hospital and a paint manufactory. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches are marked in the streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. A corner of the Vineland oval stamp sits at the top right.
notes: Park Av is today East Park Avenue.
The Freight Station label reads C.R.R. of N.J. Freight Station; the tracks are the Central Railroad of New Jersey, Southern Division.
The Park Avenue junctions with North 7th Street and North 8th Street are partly from hand-picked points (Park is 100 ft wide and drawn only to the block line).
map, 50 ft: Park to Plum, N 7th to N 8th St; CRR freight station at upper left.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 is drawn with north at the bottom of the page, so Plum is at the foot and Elmer at the head. It shows the west side of the business district at 50 ft to an inch, from South West and North West Boulevard on the left, with the double track of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad and the East Boulevards beyond it, to North 4th and South 4th Streets at the right. Three rows of blocks lie between Elmer, Landis Avenue, Wood and Plum. The blocks beside Landis Avenue are the commercial core, with the Grand Theatre (vaudeville and movies), the L.O.O.M. hall and pool room, an auction room, garages, a livery and a flour and feed store; the south side holds the West Baptist Church, a feed warehouse, printing works, a garage, the N. Borish clothing manufactory and a plumber. Wood Street is bordered by dwellings, and the Plum Street block has the Giedroyc Building with a tenant factory for clothing manufacture, a garage, a bakery, warehouses, a milk station and a row of frame dwellings. The railroad passenger station and express office stand beside the tracks at the left. The compass and the Vineland stamp appear inverted, as does all the lettering. Water pipes of 4 to 10 inches and hydrants are marked in each street.
notes: The sheet is turned about 180 degrees: north is at the bottom of the page.
Elmer is West Elmer Street here, and Plum is Plum Street, in modern names; Landis Avenue is drawn 100 ft wide.
The modern North West Boulevard line lies 3 to 4 m from the drawn line; the junctions with it carry larger residuals than those on North 4th Street.
The railroad shown is the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (today the Millville Industrial Track); its crossings were rejected as control.
map, 50 ft, turned 180 degrees (north down): Elmer to Plum, W Boulevards to N/S 4th St; Landis Av.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 shows the heart of Vineland's business district at 50 ft to an inch, from North East and South East Boulevard on the left to North 6th and South 6th Streets at the right, between Plum at the top and Elmer at the foot, with Wood and Landis Avenue between. Landis Avenue, drawn 100 ft wide, is the main street; the buildings on both sides are mostly brick stores of two and three stories with offices and lodge rooms above. West of North 6th Street are the Hotel Vineland, the bank, post office, B.P.O.E. lodge, City Hall with the fire department, the Hotel Park View and the tenant clothing manufactories, and north of Wood a group of lumber and woodworking premises (Walter E. Turner), a bottling works, a synagogue, a bakery with ovens and a water tank of 140,000 gallons capacity. East of North 6th Street stand the Masonic Temple, the Vineland Trust Co, a hall, the Vineland Vocational School and Public School No. 1 with its bicycle shed, and E. Krich & Son light manufacturing, together with the Boynton boarding house. South of Landis are the Globe Theatre, the Hotel Maretti, M. W. Garton's livery, Himes & Shover ice manufactory, the Central Fire Department and the Unitarian Church. Water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked, and the compass and Vineland stamp stand at the top right.
notes: Plum is East Plum Street in modern names; Landis Avenue is drawn 100 ft wide.
The Landis Avenue junction with the East Boulevards was not detected; the boulevard junctions at Plum, Wood and Elmer were used.
The text of the school reads Public Shool No1 as printed.
map, 50 ft: business district, Plum to Elmer, E Boulevards to 6th St; Wood, Landis Av.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 continues the business district eastward at 50 ft to an inch, from North 7th and South 7th Streets at the left to North 8th and South 8th Streets at the right edge, between Plum at the top and Elmer at the foot, with Wood and Landis Avenue between. The blocks beside Landis Avenue, drawn 100 ft wide, are filled with brick stores and shops, offices, a bakery, auto show rooms, hardware and paints stores, garages of 30 to 40 car capacity, a hall, a press room and printing office, and a bank, hotel and drug store at the left, where the Baker Ho. hotel and the Tradesmens Bank stand. The 1st M. E. Church lies north of Landis Avenue beside a row of shops, the Congl. Church of The Pilgrims lies south of Landis, and the Church of The New Jerusalem is on Wood Street. North of Wood the blocks are dwellings, with the Women's Club rooms and a small cluster of auto repair and clothing manufactory buildings at the left. The southern blocks beyond the shops are residential with a few stables and auto houses. A light manufacturing and power building and a plumber are at the left edge. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches are marked, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. The compass stands in the top left, and a corner of the Vineland stamp is at the top right.
notes: Plum is East Plum Street in modern names; Landis Avenue is drawn 100 ft wide.
North 8th Street and South 8th Street lie on the right edge, so those junctions are placed from the drawn block edge plus half the street width.
map, 50 ft: business district, Plum to Elmer, 7th to 8th St; Wood, Landis Av.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers three blocks of the west side of Vineland's business district at 50 ft to an inch, from South 4th Street along the left edge to South W. Boulevard on the right, and from Elmer Street at the top to Almond Street at the bottom, with Grape and Montrose Streets crossing between. The blocks are residential: frame dwellings of one and a half to two and a half stories fronting the east-west streets, with sheds and auto houses at the rear of the lots, one dwelling shown as a veneered house, and a few larger buildings near the boulevard end of the Montrose to Almond block. Lots are numbered along the street fronts. Four inch water pipes run in the streets, with fire hydrants at the corners. On the right the sheet shows the railroad corridor between the two boulevards: the double track of the Pennsylvania R.R., West Jersey and Seashore Division, runs down the page between South W. Boulevard and South E. Boulevard, with the narrow Penn. R.R. Freight Depot building (with its office) standing beside it. The strip east of the tracks and beyond South E. Boulevard is mostly blank and belongs to sheet 11. Streets are drawn 66 ft wide with the boulevard marked 200 ft across. The north arrow, a stamp reading June 1925, Vineland, N.J., and a scale of feet appear on the sheet; neighbouring sheet numbers 7, 20, 13 and 11 are printed in the margins.
notes: Modern names: Elmer is West Elmer Street, Grape is West Grape Street, Montrose is West Montrose Street, Almond is West Almond Street, South W. Boulevard is South West Boulevard, South E. Boulevard is South East Boulevard.
The Pennsylvania R.R. line (West Jersey and Seashore Division) between the boulevards is today's Millville Industrial Track.
map, 50 ft: Elmer to Almond, S 4th St to S W Boulevard; Grape, Montrose; Penn RR freight depot.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers three blocks of the south side of Vineland's business district at 50 ft to an inch, between South East Boulevard (the left edge, along the West Jersey and Seashore railroad) and the middle of the block east of South 6th Street, and from Elmer Street at the top to Almond Street at the bottom, with Grape and Montrose Streets crossing between. The northern two rows of blocks are residential: frame dwellings, many of one and a half to two and a half stories, with sheds and auto houses at the rear of narrow lots, a bakery on South East Boulevard and a few veneered brick houses. The southern row is industrial. West of South 6th Street, between Montrose and Almond, stand the Vineland Coat Co mill (clothing manufacture), the Joseph Bros clothing mill building and the Kimball and Prince Lumber Co with its planing mill, storage sheds, steam dry kilns, office and hardware and paints store and scattered lumber piles. East of South 6th Street the block is filled by the Chas. P. Keighley Shoe Factory, marked not in operation, with its mill buildings, warehouses, a 105,000 gallon water tank on the roof and a wagon shed, next to an airplane repairing shop with rigging and doping rooms and several vacant buildings. A railroad siding curves across the lower left corner. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches are marked in the streets, with fire hydrants and a fire alarm box at Montrose and 6th. A scale of feet is printed at the foot of the sheet.
notes: Montrose has no junction with South 6th Street in OpenStreetMap today (modern East Montrose Street).
The railroad siding at lower left belongs to the line between the East and West Boulevards (today's Millville Industrial Track).
map, 50 ft (pilot): Elmer to Almond, S E Boulevard to east of 6th St; Grape, Montrose; Vineland Coat Co, Kimball and Prince Lumber Co, Chas P Keighley Shoe Factory.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the residential and light-industrial blocks east of the Pennsylvania railroad corridor in Vineland, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. South 7th Street runs down the page left of centre and South 8th Street along the right edge, which shows only the west side of that street; Elmer Street bounds the sheet at the top and Almond Street at the bottom, with Grape and Montrose Streets crossing between. The blocks between South 7th and South 8th are mostly frame dwellings of one and a half to two and a half stories with sheds and auto houses at the rear, and a few veneered or brick-fronted houses. At the head of the block between Elmer and Grape stands Public School No. 16, heated by stove and lit by electricity, with a few dwellings around it. West of South 7th Street the blocks hold more commerce and industry: a furniture warehouse and furniture store, a candy manufactory, a warehouse, the Historical and Antiquarian Society building, and farther down Hughes Thread Co, manufacturers of silk thread, with a manufacturing and dye house, an engine room, a water tank of 5000 gallons and a private fire plant, marked as lit and powered by electricity and heated by steam. A printing shop and a paints store appear near Montrose and South 8th. A north arrow lies in the upper middle of the sheet. Streets are drawn 66 ft wide with 4 inch water pipes, and a scale of feet is printed at the foot. The Princeton University Library map division stamp is on the lower middle margin.
notes: Modern names: Elmer is Elmer Street, Grape is East Grape Street, Montrose is East Montrose Street, Almond is East Almond Street.
South 8th Street is cut by the right edge of the sheet; only its west side is drawn.
map, 50 ft: Elmer to Almond, S 7th to S 8th St; Public School No 16, Hughes Thread Co.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 shows the residential blocks south of Almond Street in Vineland, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, between South 4th Street on the left and South W. Boulevard on the right. Almond Street forms the top edge of the sheet, with only its south side drawn, and Quince and Cherry Streets cross the page at about a third and two thirds of the way down. Chestnut Avenue runs along the foot of the sheet and carries a dash-dot line marked as the borough limits, with a 4 inch water pipe beside it; the sheet ends just south of it. The blocks are filled with frame dwellings of one to two and a half stories with sheds, auto houses and coops at the rear of narrow lots, many of the dwellings veneered. Along Quince Street stand rows of similar veneered houses numbered in the 420s and 430s, and a few buildings are marked for rags storage and paper storage. A block on Cherry Street near the middle holds a vacant building and several small dwellings, and the lower blocks toward Chestnut Avenue are more thinly built, with large vacant lots. On the right the double track of the Pennsylvania R.R., West Jersey and Seashore Division, runs down the page between South W. Boulevard and South E. Boulevard, with a dwelling or two on its east side. The streets are drawn 66 ft wide except Chestnut Avenue at 100 ft and the boulevard at 200 ft. A north arrow, the June 1925 Vineland stamp and a scale of feet are on the sheet, and the left margin carries a Princeton University Library map division stamp.
notes: Modern names: Almond is West Almond Street, Quince is West Quince Street, Cherry is West Cherry Street, Chestnut Avenue is West Chestnut Avenue, South W. Boulevard is South West Boulevard, South E. Boulevard is South East Boulevard.
Chestnut Avenue junctions were not detected; control is from Almond, Quince and Cherry.
A dash-dot line along Chestnut Avenue is lettered Borough Limits.
map, 50 ft: Almond to Chestnut, S 4th St to S W Boulevard; Quince, Cherry.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers the blocks between Almond Street and Chestnut Avenue on both sides of South 6th Street in Vineland, at 50 ft to an inch, from South E. Boulevard at the left edge to the middle of the blocks east of South 6th Street. Quince Street and Cherry Street cross it. The upper left block, between Almond and Quince west of South 6th, is industrial: the Kimball and Prince Lumber Co lumber yard with its lumber sheds, piles, sash blind and door warehouse, shingle and fertilizer and cement sheds, a coal pocket with electric motor and coal pile, and Carew and Downs, coal and wood, with wagon and lime sheds, a lime tank and a private hydrant, all served by railroad sidings that curve across the block from the boulevard. J. L. Pasquale, a fruit and produce dealer, and a saw mill appear lower in the same area. East of South 6th Street, between Almond and Quince, a large mill building of Rosenthal and Dias, tenant factories for clothing manufacture, is marked with sprinklers, a wet system and watchman. The other blocks are residential: frame and veneered dwellings of one and a half to two and a half stories with outbuildings, a hardware and paints store, and, between Cherry Street and Chestnut Avenue, the Vineland Shoe Co factory marked with no watchman and no fire apparatus. Streets are 66 ft wide, with 4 and 8 inch water pipes; Chestnut Avenue at the foot is wider. A north arrow, the June 1925 stamp and a scale of feet appear on the sheet.
notes: Modern names: Almond is East Almond Street, Quince is East Quince Street, Cherry is East Cherry Street, Chestnut Avenue is East Chestnut Avenue, South E. Boulevard is South East Boulevard.
The railroad sidings in the upper left block branch from the line now called the Millville Industrial Track.
map, 50 ft: Almond to Chestnut, S E Boulevard to S 6th St; Kimball and Prince Lumber Co, Vineland Shoe Co.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers the blocks between South 6th Street and South 8th Street in Vineland at 50 ft to an inch, from Almond Street at the top to Chestnut Avenue at the foot, with Quince and Cherry Streets crossing between. South 7th Street runs down the left centre of the page and South 8th Street along the right edge, where only its west side is drawn; the left part of the sheet shows blocks west of South 7th Street out to the edge of the neighbouring sheet. Most of the sheet is residential, with frame and veneered dwellings of one and a half to two and a half stories and their sheds and auto houses. Institutional and commercial buildings are scattered through it: Sacred Heart Church, heated by steam and lit by electricity, in the upper right; a bakery with an oven and the North Italy Beneficial Assn hall on the west side of South 7th Street below Quince; feed warehouses on the east side between Quince and Cherry; a club on the south side of Cherry Street; a bottling works and a garage. The west side of South 7th Street also holds blacksmith shops and a larger veneered building near Quince. A north arrow, the June 1925 Vineland stamp and a scale of feet are on the sheet; 4 inch water pipes with fire hydrants and fire alarm boxes run in the 66 ft streets, and Chestnut Avenue is drawn wider. Sheet numbers 12, 14, 16 and 23 are printed at the margins.
notes: Modern names: Almond is East Almond Street, Quince is East Quince Street, Cherry is East Cherry Street, Chestnut Avenue is East Chestnut Avenue.
South 8th Street is cut by the right edge of the sheet; only its west side is drawn.
map, 50 ft: Almond to Chestnut, S 6th/7th to S 8th St; Sacred Heart Church.

sheet-16-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 16 is the upper two thirds of the sheet, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, and shows the ground south of Chestnut Avenue from South E. Boulevard at the left edge across South 6th Street to the middle of the block east of it. Chestnut Avenue, drawn 100 ft wide, crosses the top, with its north side cut off by the neighbouring sheet 14. The left portion is taken up by the plant of The Kiltone Co, which is marked as having a night watchman, steam heat, electric lights and power, approved automatic sprinklers, a wet system, city water supply at 60 lbs pressure and an 8 inch connection. Its buildings are numbered: storage of finished goods, an office, tank rooms for mixing and pressing, an engine room (engine not used), a dry room, a packing house, a grinding room and an acid plant with a raised section, with a laboratory and a separate storage building on the boulevard side. Railroad sidings curve in from the upper left to serve the works. A dash-dot line across the lower part of the part is lettered as the borough limits. East of the works the blocks along both sides of South 6th Street are largely vacant, with scattered dwellings, a stable and sheds, and numbered lots in the 1900s. The lower edge of the part is a heavy line, lettered no exposure, which divides it from part 2. A 4 inch water pipe runs along Chestnut Avenue and a 6 inch pipe in South 6th Street. A scale of feet and the June 1925 Vineland stamp appear on the sheet.
notes: Modern names: Chestnut Avenue is East Chestnut Avenue, South E. Boulevard is South East Boulevard.
Only two junctions (East Chestnut Avenue with South East Boulevard and South 6th Street) are drawn, so the part is a two-point helmert placement.
The dividing line with part 2 is lettered no exposure; a stretch of Chestnut Avenue east of South 6th is shown only by its south edge.
map, 50 ft: two parts split by a heavy line along Chestnut Av: part 1 S E Boulevard to S 6th (Kiltone Co), part 2 S 7th to S 8th (Limpert Bros); each placed from its two Chestnut junctions (helmert).

sheet-16-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 16 is the lower third of the sheet, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and placed on the ground east of part 1, between South 7th Street on the left and South 8th Street on the right. It shows the south side of Chestnut Avenue, a street drawn 100 ft wide whose north side is cut off by the heavy dividing line (lettered no exposure) that separates this part from part 1; the line steps down a little at the middle of the sheet. The blocks are thinly built. West of South 7th Street stands the Italian Presbyterian Church, lit by electricity and heated by hot air, with dwellings below it. Between South 7th and South 8th Streets the large block holds Limpert Bros Inc, strawberry packing department, a one-story cement-floored building with a frame gable roof, a cobbler shop and dwellings, with a stable at the head of the block; further south are rows of veneered double dwellings along South 7th Street, lettered lots in the 1800s and barns or auto sheds. A dash-dot line crossing the lower part of the sheet is the borough limits. South 8th Street, 66 ft wide at the top, narrows to 40 ft and jogs eastward at the foot of the sheet, where its lots are numbered in the 1700s. A north arrow stands near the dividing line, and a scale of feet and the Princeton University Library map division stamp are at the foot. The number 23 at the right edge marks the adjoining sheet.
notes: Modern name: Chestnut Avenue is East Chestnut Avenue.

The part has only two junctions (Chestnut Avenue with South 7th and South 8th Streets), so it is a two-point helmert placement; the South 8th Street junction lies about 25 ft north of the dividing line and was hand-picked.
A 40 ft jog in South 8th Street at the foot of the sheet is drawn; its modern line was not checked.
map, 50 ft: two parts split by a heavy line along Chestnut Av: part 1 S E Boulevard to S 6th (Kiltone Co), part 2 S 7th to S 8th (Limpert Bros); each placed from its two Chestnut junctions (helmert).

sheet-17-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 17 is the main map of the sheet, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, and shows the ground south of Chestnut Avenue along the Pennsylvania railroad corridor on the southern edge of Vineland's built-up area. Chestnut Avenue, 100 ft wide, crosses the top, and a dash-dot line along it and then down the middle of the sheet marks the borough limits. On the right side runs the 200 ft corridor of South W. Boulevard and South E. Boulevard with the Pennsylvania R.R. (West Jersey and Seashore Division) track between them; the lots along its west side are numbered in the 2000s. Most of the sheet is open ground in large blocks, with a few scattered buildings: F. Defalco, coal and wood, with its storage shed and lumber sheds near Chestnut Avenue; dwellings and barns at the upper left, where the sheet number 20 marks the adjoining sheet; the Vineland Foundry Co, a one-story foundry with a cupola and pattern storage, marked with light and power electric, no heat, no watchman and no fire apparatus. In the lower half the Consolidated Glass Co, marked not in operation, occupies the large works served by a railroad siding that branches from the main line: the glass tube alley, a glass furnace, glory holes, lehrs, a batch room, gas producers, a storage shed, an engine and belt room with an office, a buried 12,000 gallon oil tank and a sand shed. The lower left corner of the sheet is occupied by a heavy-bordered box (no exposure) that is a separate part of the sheet and is not covered here. A north arrow, the June 1925 stamp and a scale of feet appear.
notes: Modern names: Chestnut Avenue is West Chestnut Avenue and East Chestnut Avenue either side of the boulevards, South W. Boulevard is South West Boulevard, South E. Boulevard is South East Boulevard.

Only one junction (South West Boulevard with Chestnut Avenue) could be hand-picked; the part is placed by that point and a derived point at the neighbouring sheets' scale and rotation, so its position is low confidence.
The railroad corridor between the boulevards is today's Millville Industrial Track; the drawn corridor is 200 ft wide.

map, 50 ft: part 1 south of Chestnut between S W Boulevard and the railroad (Vineland Foundry Co, Consolidated Glass Co), one hand-picked point plus a derived one; part 2 boxed at lower left (block 56) not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: boxed part at lower left: block 56, west side of S W Boulevard, lots 2001 to 2004 (no street junction; only the boulevard runs through it; needs a point carried from sheet-20 or sheet-13 (block 56), or position along the boulevard from lot numbers).

sheet-18-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 18, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the north-western edge of the borough above Park Avenue, which is drawn 100 ft wide with the borough limits running along it. The lettered streets are North 2nd, North 3rd and North 4th Streets, France and Erin, and the North West Boulevard at the right edge. Between North 3rd and North 4th Streets the block north of France is filled by the Vineland Basket Co, with basket storage sheds, a wood working building and a night watchman noted. The blocks between Erin and Park Avenue (B5, B6) hold scattered frame dwellings, coops, sheds and a few greenhouses and florist buildings; the area west of North 3rd Street (B1) is mostly open, with a row of small houses and coops along Park Avenue. At the top right of the sheet, beyond a long blank area marked only by the block number B2, are the buildings of the New Jersey Home for Disabled Soldiers, Sailors or Marines and their Wives: a fireproof reinforced concrete hospital built in 1914, cottages, storage buildings, barns and a long blue-coloured building, with a note on its fire protection. Water pipes of 4 inches and fire hydrants are marked along Park Avenue and the boulevard. The part ends at a heavy line below Park Avenue; the strip below it is part 2, a different area east of the railroad.
notes: France is today Lafrance Street. The modern junction of Lafrance Street and North 4th Street lies about 40 m from where the sheet draws France and 4th, so it was left out.
Park Avenue is drawn 100 ft wide along the borough limits (modern West Park Avenue).

map, 100 ft: two parts split by a heavy line: top, NJ Home for Disabled Soldiers, France, Erin, Park Av west of the railroad; bottom, Cambridge Av to Park Av east of the railroad (Park Drive, Crystal, Harvard, Gilmore, N East Av).

sheet-18-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 18, drawn at 100 ft to an inch below a heavy line, covers the strip north of Park Avenue and east of the railroad, between Cambridge Avenue (the borough limits) at the top and Park Avenue at the bottom, from Park Drive in the west to beyond North East Avenue and the borough line in the east. The Central Railroad of New Jersey (Southern Division) crosses diagonally near the left edge, between Park Drive and Crystal Avenue, with a basket warehouse beside it. The cross streets are Park Drive, Crystal Avenue, Harvard, Gilmore and North East Avenue, with blocks numbered 3A, 4A, 5A, 82 and 83. The area is lightly built: frame dwellings, sheds, coops and auto houses, a Standard Oil Co plant near Cambridge Avenue and Crystal Avenue, the Vineland Scientific Glass Co (fireproof fused mica building and warehouse) on Cambridge Avenue east of the railroad, and a stone cutting yard near North East Avenue. Park Avenue is drawn 100 ft wide with 6 and 8 inch water pipes; below it are the openings of North 7th Street, North 8th Street, North East Avenue and Myrtle Street, which belong to sheets 6 and 22. A scale bar reading 100 ft to one inch is printed at the foot.
notes: Cambridge Avenue is today Cambridge Street; Harvard and Gilmore are Harvard Street and Gilmore Street; Park Avenue here is East Park Avenue.
The junction of Park Avenue and Harvard was measured 7 m off (a lot line) and rejected; Park Drive at Park Avenue was not detected.

map, 100 ft: two parts split by a heavy line: top, NJ Home for Disabled Soldiers, France, Erin, Park Av west of the railroad; bottom, Cambridge Av to Park Av east of the railroad (Park Drive, Crystal, Harvard, Gilmore, N East Av).

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 covers the north-west quarter of Vineland's central grid at 100 ft to an inch, from Park Avenue along the top to Elmer along the bottom, and from North and South West Avenue at the left edge to North and South 4th Street near the right edge. Landis Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet, with Wood, Plum, Pear and Peach Streets running east and west above it. The upper third of the sheet is thinly built: large blocks between Park Avenue and Pear Street hold scattered frame dwellings, a sketched compass rose and north arrow, and Public School No. 8 near North 2nd Street, with the borough limits drawn as a dash-dot line across the top. A railroad track runs east and west along Pear Street, with a curved siding turning in to the Municipal Water Works, Power and Light Station on the west side of North 2nd Street, which has an engine room, boiler house, water cooler, storage sheds and a sewage disposal building. A Boro Garage stands on the block east of the works. Below Plum Street the blocks fill with small frame dwellings on narrow lots, then with denser dwellings, shops, a cooperage and an A.M.E. church west of North 2nd Street, and a mix of dwellings, stores and small factories along Landis Avenue, which is drawn 100 ft wide. South of Landis the blocks are again mostly dwellings, down to Elmer at the foot of the sheet. Water pipes of 4, 6, 8 and 10 inches are marked in the streets with fire hydrants. The sheet number 19 is printed in the corners, with adjoining sheet numbers in the margins.
notes: West Avenue is North West Avenue and South West Avenue in OpenStreetMap; East Park Avenue is West Park Avenue here, Elmer is West Elmer Street.
Street names on the sheet were read from the 1600 px overview and a few full-resolution crops; spellings and the Elmer label should be rechecked.
Pear Street carries the Vineland Running Track; its junctions are about 7 m off and were rejected.
map, 100 ft: Park Av to Elmer, West Av to 4th St; railroad in Pear St.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 covers the south-west quarter of Vineland's central grid at 100 ft to an inch, from Elmer along the top to Chestnut Avenue near the foot, and from South West Avenue at the left edge to South 4th Street near the right edge. Grape, Montrose, Almond, Quince and Cherry Streets cross it east and west, with South 2nd and South 3rd Streets running down the sheet. The blocks are largely residential, filled with small frame dwellings on narrow lots with sheds and auto houses at the rear, thinning towards the west and south where whole blocks are open or hold only a few houses. The West Side Public School stands in the upper middle of the sheet near South 3rd Street, and another public school stands in the lower left corner block, west of South 2nd Street. Near the right edge between Almond and Quince the Vineland Clothing Co occupies a block with a large factory building and a water tank. A few stores and small shops are scattered along the east side of South 4th Street, and a handful of larger buildings sit in the blocks south of Quince. A compass rose with a north arrow is drawn at the left edge near Grape. A dash-dot line near the foot of the sheet along Chestnut Avenue is the borough limit. Water pipes, fire hydrants and a few alarm boxes are marked in the streets. Sheet 20 is printed in the top corners, with neighbouring sheet numbers in the margins and a scale bar near the foot.
notes: Modern names: West Elmer Street, West Grape Street, West Montrose Street, West Almond Street, West Quince Street, West Cherry Street, West Chestnut Avenue; South West Avenue keeps its name.
Street names were read from the 1600 px overview with a few full-resolution crops; recheck spellings.
map, 100 ft: Elmer to Chestnut Av, West Av to 4th St.

sheet-21-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 21, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, is an L-shaped area on the western edge of Vineland, west of the borough line on West Avenue: a strip along Landis Avenue (drawn 100 ft wide) running west from West Avenue across the whole width of the sheet, and a narrow strip along the west side of West Avenue from above Landis Avenue south to Quince Street. A heavy line, marked no exposure, separates it from part 2 below. Along Landis Avenue the lots carry house numbers 2501 to 2554; the frontage is thinly built with frame dwellings, auto houses, coops, a filling station at West Avenue, an auto body manufacturing building of concrete block and a veneered store building with three shops near the corner of West Avenue. The West Avenue strip is block 1A, with scattered dwellings, coops, sheds and a vacant factory. West Avenue is drawn 100 ft wide with the borough limits along its centre line; on its east side only the ends of the cross streets are shown, lettered Wood Street, Elmer Street, Grape Street, Montrose Street, Almond Street and Quince Street, with the numbers of the adjoining sheets 19 and 20. Water pipes, fire hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked on West Avenue and Landis Avenue. A large compass rose stands at the left edge of the sheet.
notes: West Avenue keeps its name today (North and South West Avenue).
The part is placed from six junctions along West Avenue (Wood, Landis, Elmer, Grape, Montrose, Quince); the Landis Avenue strip west of West Avenue has no cross street and no control of its own.

map, 100 ft, two parts split by heavy lines: part 1 Landis Av strip west of West Av plus the west side of West Av from Wood to Quince; part 2 west of S West Av from Quince to south of Chestnut Av (Walter E Fernald Foundry). Both placed along West Avenue only (helmert).

sheet-21-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 21, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers open land west of South West Avenue between Quince Street and the area south of Chestnut Avenue, on the western edge of Vineland outside the borough. South West Avenue and Chestnut Avenue are both drawn 100 ft wide; Quince Street and Cherry Street are lettered only as short stubs on the east side of South West Avenue, in a narrow strip of block 20 between the avenue and a heavy line on the right. The large blocks numbered 1A, 21 and 54 are thinly built: frame dwellings, auto houses, many coops and sheds along Chestnut Avenue and South West Avenue, with house numbers 2301 to 2335. Near the lower right is the Walter E Fernald Foundry, a small building noted as having no watchman, electric lights and no fire apparatus. A 4 inch water pipe runs in South West Avenue. A scale bar reading 100 ft to one inch is printed at the foot of the sheet.
notes: Chestnut Avenue is today West Chestnut Avenue; Quince Street and Cherry Street are West Quince Street and West Cherry Street.

Placed from one hand-picked junction (South West Avenue and Chestnut Avenue) plus a derived point along the drawn West Avenue at the atlas scale and grid rotation; three hand-picked junctions along West Avenue disagreed by 3.5 m and were dropped.

map, 100 ft, two parts split by heavy lines: part 1 Landis Av strip west of West Av plus the west side of West Av from Wood to Quince; part 2 west of S West Av from Quince to south of Chestnut Av (Walter E Fernald Foundry). Both placed along West Avenue only (helmert).

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 covers the north-east quarter of Vineland's central grid at 100 ft to an inch, from Park Avenue at the top to Elmer at the foot, and from 8th Street at the left edge to State Street and Virginia Avenue at the right. Peach, Pear, Plum, Wood and Landis Avenue cross it east and west, with East Avenue and Myrtle Street running down the middle. The built-up part is the western third, where 8th Street and the streets about it are filled with close-set frame dwellings, with a public school near Park Avenue and 8th Street, two churches and a church school between Wood and Landis, and brick stores, a church and tall brick buildings facing Landis Avenue and South 8th Street at the lower left. East of East Avenue the blocks are largely open: a few scattered dwellings, a farm-like group of buildings between Myrtle Street and Ewan Terrace, a parochial school south of the compass rose on East Avenue, and a larger house and grounds near Landis Avenue and State Street. The streets east of Myrtle are lightly built, with Ewan Terrace and Arcadia Place only partly lined with houses. Virginia Avenue runs down the right margin. A compass rose and north arrow stand in the upper middle, and a scale bar and the Vineland, N.J. cartouche dated June 1925 are in the corners. Landis and Park Avenues are drawn 100 ft wide. Water pipes and hydrants are marked in the streets. Sheet numbers 18, 22, 23, 24 and 25 appear in the margins as the adjoining sheets.
notes: Modern names: East Park Avenue, East Plum Street, Pear Street and New Pear Street, Elmer Street; East Avenue is North East Avenue and South East Avenue.
Virginia Avenue junctions were rejected by the fit (about 12 m) and left out.
Street names were read from the 1600 px overview with a few full-resolution crops; recheck spellings.
map, 100 ft: Park Av to Elmer, 8th St to State St; Virginia Av left out (11 to 12 m off); fit scale about 3.97 px/ft.

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 covers the south-east quarter of Vineland's central grid at 100 ft to an inch, scanned on a tan paper tone. It runs from Elmer at the top to Chestnut Avenue near the foot, and from 8th Street, a little inside the left edge, to State Street at the right. Grape, Montrose, Almond, Quince and Cherry cross it east and west; East Avenue, Myrtle Avenue and, in the upper right, Arcadia Place run down the sheet. The western part, between 8th Street and East Avenue, is closely built with frame dwellings on regular lots, a few brick stores and a church at the lower left, and Public School No. 6 in the block between Cherry and Chestnut Avenue. The East Public School, a large pink building, stands on the east side of East Avenue between Montrose and Almond, and a church building stands at the top near Elmer. East of East Avenue the blocks are more loosely built: dwellings strung along Myrtle Avenue, a few larger buildings at Michigan Avenue, and mostly open ground east of Arcadia Place, which is lined with only a few houses. A strip of long narrow lots runs along both sides of Myrtle Avenue. A compass rose stands at the right edge. The foot of the sheet is crossed by Chestnut Avenue, drawn 100 ft wide, with a row of dwellings and a few stores beyond it. Block numbers and the numbers of neighbouring sheets are printed in the left margin, the cartouche is at upper right, and a scale bar and the Princeton library stamp at the bottom right.
notes: Modern names: East Grape Street, East Montrose Street, East Almond Street, East Quince Street, East Cherry Street, East Chestnut Avenue; Myrtle Avenue is South Myrtle Street; Arcadia Drive is probably today's Chambers Place.
The fit gave px_per_ft 3.976 against about 3.93 on the western sheets; the sheet may be drawn slightly oversize (scale_ft about 99).
Street names were read from the 1600 px overview with a few full-resolution crops; recheck spellings.
map, 100 ft, tan scan: Elmer to Chestnut Av, 8th St to State St (East Av, Myrtle Av, Michigan Av, Arcadia Drive).

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 covers the north-east part of the central grid at 100 ft to an inch, from Park Avenue at the top to Landis Avenue and the first row of blocks south of it, and from Virginia Avenue at the left edge to Valley Avenue and Victory Avenue at the right. Pear Street and, in the upper right, New Pear run east and west across it. Most of the sheet is sparsely built: the large block between Pear Street and Landis Avenue is taken up by the long pink poultry houses of the Wene Chick Farm, with chicken coops and a farm dwelling, and a small cluster of dwellings and a shop lies north of Pear Street near Virginia Avenue. Kerr Avenue, a narrow lane, runs north from Landis Avenue through open ground toward the farm and a group of poultry houses and sheds. East of Valley Avenue, long narrow lots on both sides of North Valley Avenue and Victory Avenue hold scattered dwellings. Along the foot of the sheet, south of Landis Avenue, a row of blocks is built with frame dwellings between Howard Street, Columbia Avenue, Deshibe Terrace, and South Valley Avenue. A compass rose and north arrow are at the upper right, with the Vineland, N.J. cartouche dated June 1925 and a scale bar. Landis Avenue and Park Avenue are drawn 100 ft wide. Sheet 24 is printed in both upper corners.
notes: Modern names: East Park Avenue, New Pear Street, North Valley Avenue and South Valley Avenue, Landis Avenue, Howard Street, Columbia Avenue; Deshibe Terrace is probably today's D'Shibe Terrace.

The fit gave px_per_ft 4.005 against about 3.93 on the western sheets (about 2 percent), with residuals of 2.5 to 3 m on the two Landis Avenue junctions at Columbia and Valley; the sheet may be drawn slightly oversize (scale_ft about 98).
Street names were read from the 1600 px overview; recheck spellings, in particular Kerr, Deshibe and the abbreviations.
map, 100 ft: Park Av to Landis, Virginia Av to Victory Av (Kerr, New Pear, Wene Chick Farm); fit scale 4.0 px/ft.

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 covers the south-east part of the central grid at 100 ft to an inch, from Landis Avenue and the blocks below it at the top to Chestnut Avenue at the foot, and from State Street at the left edge to Valley Avenue and the streets beyond it at the right. Almond runs east and west across the middle of the sheet and Cherry crosses the lower left, with Howard Street, Columbia Avenue, Deshibe Terrace, Louisa Avenue and Valley Avenue running down the sheet. The upper half is a district of narrow, deep lots along Howard Street, Columbia Avenue and Deshibe Terrace, built with small frame dwellings and outbuildings, with a few larger houses and a brick or concrete store near the middle. Below Almond the sheet is more open: scattered dwellings along Columbia Avenue and Louisa Avenue, a private road running east from Columbia Avenue, and large unbuilt blocks, with a hospital building and annex standing in the open block at the left near Cherry. Valley Avenue forms a built-up strip with dwellings and sheds at the right. Chestnut Avenue, drawn 100 ft wide, crosses the foot of the sheet; below it, a row of dwellings faces the street. A compass rose and north arrow are at the upper right, the Vineland, N.J. cartouche dated June 1925 above it, and a scale bar and the Princeton library stamp at the bottom. Block numbers and the numbers of adjoining sheets 22, 23 and 24 are printed in the margins.
notes: Modern names: East Almond Street, East Chestnut Avenue, South Valley Avenue, Howard Street, Columbia Avenue; Deshibe Terrace is probably today's D'Shibe Terrace.
Cherry and South State Street were left out of the fit: the modern Cherry Street east of State lies about 40 m from the drawn Cherry, and State Street junctions were 4 to 7 m off.
Street names were read from the 1600 px overview; recheck spellings.
map, 100 ft: Landis to Chestnut Av, State St to Valley Av (Howard, Columbia, Deshibe Ter, Louisa Av); weak, Cherry and S State St left out.
